preamble: Insertion of the voiced dental fricative [ð] is rare. It occurs in Spanish through hypercorrection. Colloquial Spanish drops intervocalic /d/ in the participle ending -ado (cansado > cansao), so speakers who restore the d sometimes add one to words that never had it, giving bacalado for bacalao and Bilbado for Bilbao. Because Spanish spirantizes /d/ between vowels, the inserted consonant is pronounced [ð̞].
